subject.title: feat(talk): enable GPT Live with Codex OAuth

question: Should OpenClaw support a public Plugin SDK registrar for plugin-owned browser realtime session brokers, or should the Codex OAuth route remain an internal bundled-provider implementation?
rationale: This is a durable cross-plugin API and auth/session ownership decision, not a mechanical correctness choice; the branch’s runtime design is plausible, but maintainers must choose the permanent extension boundary before external consumers can rely on it.

options.title: Approve the generic broker seam
options.body: Accept the registrar as a supported Plugin SDK contract and review its ownership, lifecycle, and compatibility guarantees before landing.

options.title: Keep it bundled-only
options.body: Replace the public registrar with an internal bundled-runtime seam so the Codex OAuth feature does not create a new external plugin API.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic broker seam
recommendation.body: Accept the registrar as a supported Plugin SDK contract and review its ownership, lifecycle, and compatibility guarantees before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch author is the available technical contact for explaining the proposed broker contract; a repository owner still needs to make the product/API decision.
